title: Use Reverse Q&A to Learn What's Really Going On
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece diagnoses a structural problem in how information travels inside organizations: team members filter what they tell leaders because they want to be viewed favorably, so problems often stay hidden until they're too big to ignore. Standard Q&A sessions, where leaders answer questions from the team, don't fully solve this because they don't compel anyone to surface bad news. The proposed fix is "Reverse Q&A" — leaders proactively asking small groups a consistent set of probing questions (what am I blind to, what's undermining performance, what needs to change) rather than waiting to be told. Run alongside normal open forums, the practice is presented as a way to systematically unlock candor that top-down communication alone can't reach.
points: Team members are described as filtering information upward because they want to be viewed favorably by those who can reward or punish them.
Standard Q&A, where leaders answer questions, is distinguished from "Reverse Q&A," where leaders proactively ask small groups a consistent set of probing questions.
Reverse Q&A questions are specific and repeatable: what is the leader blind to, what undermines effectiveness, what needs to change, what's the best and worst of the organization.
Running Reverse Q&A alongside large open forums is presented as the combination that most effectively unlocks organization-wide candor.
quotes: Even in the best organizations, information about problems and issues faced by others travels slowly upward.
Because team members want to be viewed favorably by those who can reward and punish them, they filter information about problems, giving leaders less truth about the organization than they desire.
So, the best leaders go one step further. They engage in Reverse Q&A.

Leaders learn what they need to know when they ask small groups of team members what the leader might be blind to, what is getting in the way of team effectiveness, what needs to change to promote the highest performance.
By engaging in Reverse Q&A sessions continually throughout the year, leaders soon crack the code that unlocks candid communication.
Creating open communication in every direction is the real work of leadership.
